$comment: Generated from crates/protocol by crates/protocol-schema; do not edit. Run `make protocol`.

Access.description: What a data grant allows on the documents it covers.

oneOf.description: Query, get, search and watch them, read their history and blobs.

Update, splice and delete them (and read them). A changed document must
still be covered by the grant.
Create documents of the type; each must be covered by the grant's filter.

AdoptApp.description: An app's connection: its messages are stamped with this reverse-DNS app id.

AdoptParams.description:
Params of `adopt`, with which session hands the broker one end of a socket
pair (the request's one descriptor) and says what the connection is.

AdoptResult.description: Result of `adopt`: the new connection's number.

AdoptSystem.description: A system service's connection: it may claim names and tap the bus.

AppsResult.description: Result of `apps`: the apps session is running.

AtParams.description: Params of `at`: document `id` as it was just after change set `change_set`.

AuditAction.description: What happened, in an audit entry.

oneOf.description: A grant was made.
A grant was removed.
The user turned down a request.

AuditEntry.description: One entry in the audit log.

at.description: When, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

by.description: Who did it: `user`, or a service, tool or app.

AuditParams.description: Params of `audit`: the most recent entries.

blobs_copied.description: Blobs copied this time; the rest were on the drive already.

bytes_copied.description: Bytes copied this time, the database included.

BacklinkInfo.description: A link into a document from another live document.

bytes.description: The database copy's size; its blobs are shared and not counted.

change_set.description: The newest change set it holds.

device.description: The device it's of (its database's peer id, in hex).

taken.description: When it was taken, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

BackupStatus.description: Everything backupd knows: the drives, and what it's doing.

error.description: Why the last backup or restore failed, until the next one succeeds.

BackupsResult.description: Result of `backups`: every backup on the drive, newest first.

created.description: When it was first stored, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

refs.description: How many fields of live documents refer to it.

BrokerErrorCode.description: Error codes the broker itself sends. Services may send their own.

oneOf.description: The frame was valid JSON but the message makes no sense (unknown method, bad params).
No connection has claimed the name the request was sent to.
Another connection already holds the name.
The permission hook refused the message.
The service didn't answer within the request's timeout.
The service disconnected before answering.
The connection is at one of the broker's per-connection limits (pending requests, subscriptions or names).

BusError.description: Why a request failed. `code` is one of the broker's codes or a service's own.

Busy.description: A backup or restore in progress.

ChangeKind.description: What a change set did to a document.

oneOf.description: Undoing a delete brought it back.

ChangeSetInfo.description: One write, possibly to several documents.

docs.description: Ids of the documents it touched.

ChangesParams.description: Params of `changes`: the most recent change sets.

limit.description: At most this many (default 100, at most 10,000).

CheckStyleParams.description: Params of `check_style`: a style sheet to check, as the compositor parses them.

CheckStyleResult.description: Result of `check_style`: what's wrong with the sheet, if anything.

Clipboard.description: What's on the clipboard: text, and the document it came from, if any.

CompactResult.description:
Result of `compact`: what history compaction removed. Everything from the last
30 days stays; older, the last version of each day, and after a year, of each
week. Then blobs nothing needs any more are deleted.

change_sets.description: Change sets left with no versions, removed.

ConnectParams.description:
Params of `connect`: join `ssid`, with `password` if it's secure and not
known yet.

ip4.description: Its IPv4 address, with prefix length, if it has one yet.

name.description: Its name: the Wi-Fi network's, or the wired profile's.

DataRule.description: Access to documents of one type.

filter.description:
Only documents matching this filter (the database's query language).
Empty covers every document of the type.

DiffParams.description:
Params of `diff`: document `id` from just after change set `from` (0 for
before it was created) to just after change set `to`.

created.description: When it was created, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

id.description: A UUIDv7, so ids sort by creation time.

updated.description: When it last changed, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

Drive.description: A drive backupd can use: a plugged-in exFAT drive.

free.description: Free space, in bytes, when last looked at.

id.description: How methods name it: its block device (`sda1`).

last.description: This device's newest backup on it.

set_up.description: Whether it's a backup drive (it holds an `idealos-backup` folder).

FieldChangeInfo.description:
One field that differs. Objects are compared field by field, arrays and other
values as a whole.

after.description: Absent when the field doesn't exist after.

before.description: Absent when the field didn't exist before.

by.description:
Who granted it: `user` (a prompt), or the service, tool or app that called
`grant`.

granted.description: When, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

GrantParams.description: Params of `grant`: give app `app` these rules, without asking the user.

app.description: Only this app's grants. (An app always gets only its own.)

GrantsResult.description: Result of `grants` and `grant`, and the data published on `GRANTS_TOPIC`.

version.description:
Grows with every change (it survives restarts), so a follower that gets
tables out of order keeps the newest.

HelloResult.description: Result of `hello`: who the broker says this connection is.

sender.description: How the broker stamps this connection's messages.

HistoryResult.description: Result of `history`: every change to the document, oldest first.

InfoResult.description: Result of `info`: about this device and system.

kernel.description: The kernel's name and release, such as `Linux 6.12.58`.

services.description: Services session is running, by name.

LinkInfo.description: A link out of a document.

exists.description: Whether the target exists (and isn't deleted).

path.description: The field holding the link, such as `from.contact` or `tracks.3`.

connections.description: How many connections the broker has.

services.description: Each claimed service name and the connection that holds it.

ListResult2.description: Result of `list`: the names of the caller's secrets.

fds.description: How many file descriptors travel with this message (see `unix`).

stream.description:
Ask for a streamed answer: the service may send any number of
`Stream` frames before its response, and the request has no
timeout. It stays open until the service responds, the requester
cancels, or either side disconnects.

timeout_ms.description: Overrides `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`. Not allowed on a streamed request.

oneOf.description:
One part of a streamed answer to request `id`, from the service it went to.
The broker forwards it under the requester's id; the request stays open.

The requester no longer wants the answer to request `id`. The broker
forwards it to the service and drops the response if one still comes.

`topic` is an exact topic, or a prefix ending in `.*` (see
`topic_matches`). The broker answers with a response carrying `id`.

name.description: A service name: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `.`.

oneOf.description: Online.
Joining a network.
Connected to a network with no route to the internet.
No network manager to ask.

NetStatus.description: Result of `status`, and each part of `watch`.

wifi_present.description: Whether there's a Wi-Fi device at all.

rescan.description: Scan first (takes a few seconds), rather than list what was last seen.

NetworksResult.description: Result of `networks`: strongest first, one entry per name.

NodeKind.description:
Node types understood by the compositor: primitives (`group`, `rect`, `text`,
`image`), containers that lay out their children (`vstack`, `hstack`,
`toolbar`, `grid`, `split`, `scroll`, `dialog`), and widgets the compositor
draws and drives itself (`label`, `button`, `checkbox`, `toggle`, `slider`,
`select`, `menu`, `text_field`, `text_area`, `vlist`, `terminal`).

oneOf.description:
A button labelled `label` that opens a menu of `options`; choosing one
sends a `choose` event with it. Unlike a select, it keeps no value.

A virtual list: `count` rows of `row_height`, of which the app creates only
the visible ones (it hears which, as `range` events), each with an `index`.

A terminal showing pty session `pty` (see `pty`), which the app
opened. The compositor attaches to the session as the app, draws its
screen, and sends it what's typed and the size that fits; the app sees
none of it.

OpenParams.description: Params of `open`: the screen's starting size.

app.description:
The app's id, as its app-host says. Used only when the broker gave the
connection no app identity (an app run by hand on a Mac, with no session),
to match the window to edits of that app's style sheet.

style.description:
The app's style sheet: CSS-like rules for colours and fonts, applied inside
the window over the system's (see the compositor's `style` module). At most
64 KiB; a sheet with a mistake fails `open_window`, saying where.

width.description: Size of the content area in logical pixels (default 360 by 240).

OrderBy.description:
A sort key: a field path (or `$updated`, `$created`) and a direction,
written `["date", "desc"]`.

PinParams.description:
Params of `pin`: pin (or with `pinned` false, unpin) document `id`'s version
after change set `change_set`, so history compaction keeps it.

PromptParams.description:
Params of `prompt`: app `app` (called `name`) asks for these things, each in
words (see `describe`), for `reason`.

PutParams.description: Params of `put`: store `value` as `name`, replacing what was there.

Query.description: A query: documents of one type that match a filter, in order.

limit.description: At most this many documents (default 100, at most 10,000).

offset.description: Skip this many matching documents first.

orderBy.description:
Sort keys, most significant first: field paths, or `$updated` and
`$created` for when a document last changed and when it was made. Ties
keep creation order.

where.description:
Field paths mapped to a value to equal or an object of operators (`$eq`,
`$ne`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$in`, `$nin`, `$exists`, `$contains`),
plus `$and`, `$or` and `$not`, and on the whole document `$id`,
`$createdBy`, `$linksTo` and `$linkedFrom`. Empty matches every document
of the type.

RequestParams.description: Params of `request`: what the app would like, and why, in its own words.

granted.description:
Whether the app now has everything it asked for (because the user allowed
it, or it already had it).

RestoreBackupParams.description:
Params of `restore`: replace the database with backup `name` from `drive`,
bringing its blobs back too. The state replaced is kept as a snapshot, so the
restore can be undone. A backup of another device makes this device that one.

RestoreParams.description: Params of `restore`: replace the database with snapshot `name`.

adopt.description:
Take a snapshot of another device's database too, and become that device.
backupd sets it to restore a backup onto a new device.

RestoreResult.description:
Result of `restore`: the snapshot of the state it replaced, so restoring that
one undoes the restore.

RevokeParams.description: Params of `revoke`: the grants with these ids, and every grant of `app`.

Run.description: A run of cells on one row that look alike.

SceneOp.description: One change to a window's scene graph.

oneOf.description: Merge `props` into the node's existing props.

SchemasResult.description: Result of `schemas`: each system type's JSON Schema.

ScreenFrame.description: One part of `attach`'s streamed answer: the screen, or what changed on it.

app_cursor.description: The arrow keys should send application-mode sequences (`ESC O A`).

bracketed_paste.description: Pasted text should be wrapped in `ESC [200~` ... `ESC [201~`.

cursor.description: Where the cursor is (row, column), or absent while it's hidden.

lines.description:
Changed rows: each row's index and its runs, left to right. A row's runs
cover it from the first column; the rest of the row is blank.

ScreenInfo.description: Result of `screen`: the display, in logical pixels.

SearchParams.description: Params of `search`: documents containing every word of `text`, best first.

limit.description: At most this many (default 100, at most 10,000).

Sender.description: Who sent a message, as stamped by the broker.

oneOf.description: A system service that claimed a well-known name such as `db`.
An app, identified by its app id and bus connection number.

A trusted local connection (a tool such as `osctl`, or a service before it
claims a name), identified by its bus connection number.
The first part: the session's id, for `attach` and the `terminal` node.
The shell set the window title.

The shell exited, with this status (or the signal that ended it, negated).
The stream ends after this.

change_set.description: The newest change set it holds.

taken.description: When it was taken, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

SpliceParams.description:
Params of `splice`: edit the text at field `path` (dotted, such as `body` or
`notes.summary`) of document `id`: at character `at`, delete `delete`
characters, then insert `insert`. The field becomes collaborative text (it reads
as a plain string everywhere), so concurrent edits merge and each splice is its
own change in history. Positions count Unicode characters, not bytes.

StatsResult.description:
Result of `stats`: how much the database holds. Needs the `storage`
capability (or a system caller).

db_bytes.description: The database file, with its write-ahead log.

device.description: This device, as backups name it: its database's peer id, in hex.

StyleError.description: A mistake in a style sheet, and where it is (1-based).

SystemStyleResult.description: Result of `system_style`: the built-in system style sheet, for reference.

SystemTrust.description: The one trust level `adopt` names explicitly.

TapEvent.description: The data of each publish on the tap topic: one message the broker received.

bus_id.description:
For a request the broker forwards: the id the service sees and answers
with, to match the request to its response in the trace.

conn.description: The connection the message came from.

msg.description: The message as the connection sent it (before the broker rewrote its id).

TypesResult.description:
Result of `types`: every document type with live documents the caller may
read, and how many, by name.

UndoParams.description:
Params of `undo`: revert change set `change_set` with a new change set. Undoing
an undo redoes.

UndoResult.description: Result of `undo`: the change set the undo made.

UpdateParams.description:
Params of `update`: a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) for document `id`. A key set
to null is removed, an object merges into the object there, and anything else
replaces the old value.

VersionInfo.description: One change set's effect on one document.

at.description: When, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

origin.description: Who: the service name or app id that made the change.

pinned.description: Pinned: history compaction never removes it.

undoes.description: The change set this one undid, if it was an undo.

WatchEvent.description:
A part of `watch`'s streamed answer.

To keep a list up to date: drop the `removed` ids, replace the `changed`
documents, append the `added` ones, and then, if `order` is present, sort the
list to match it.

oneOf.description: The first part: every matching document, in order.
What changed since the previous part.

added.description: Documents that are now in the result and weren't before.

changed.description: Documents still in the result whose contents changed.

order.description:
Every id in the result, in order. Present whenever the order isn't
just the previous one with the removed ids taken out (so whenever
something was added or moved).

removed.description:
Ids of documents no longer in the result (deleted, no longer matching,
or pushed past the limit).

active.description: The device is on it now.

known.description: Joined before: its password is saved.

oneOf.description: The first part: the window's id, for commits, and its content size.

Something happened to node `node` (an id from the app's commits): `click`
(a button it listens to), `change` (a widget's new value: a checkbox's or
toggle's boolean, a slider's number, a select's option, a text field's text),
`submit` (Enter in a text field, with its text), `range` (a virtual list's
visible rows, as `[first, last]`), `choose` (a menu's chosen option), or
`cancel` (Escape in a dialog).
The window's content area changed size (the user resized or maximized it).

The user asked to close the window. It stays until the app cancels the
request (or answers it).

WriteParams.description:
Params of `write`: bytes for the shell, as text (keys are text, or escape
sequences, which are too).

description: Bus frames are a 4-byte big-endian length followed by one UTF-8 JSON `Message`.
title: idealos wire protocol

BROKER.description: The broker's own name: `hello`, `claim`, `release` and `list` go to it, and `adopt`, with which session hands it connections for services and apps.

DB_SERVICE.description: The name the database service claims.

DEFAULT_QUERY_LIMIT.description: The `limit` a query gets when it names none.

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS.description: How long the broker waits for a response before answering `timeout` itself, unless the request sets `timeout_ms`.

GRANTS_TOPIC.description: Where permd publishes every grant whenever they change.

MAX_FDS_PER_MESSAGE.description: Most file descriptors one message may carry.

MAX_FRAME_BYTES.description: Largest frame the broker accepts, not counting the 4-byte length prefix.

MAX_NAMES.description: Most service names one connection may claim.

MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS.description: Most requests one connection may have waiting for an answer at once; past it the broker answers `limit_exceeded`.

MAX_QUERY_LIMIT.description: Most documents one query returns; a larger `limit` is an error.

MAX_STREAMS.description: Most streamed requests one connection may have open at once; they don't count against `MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS`.

MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS.description: Most subscription patterns one connection may hold.

MAX_TIMEOUT_MS.description: Longest `timeout_ms` the broker honors; longer ones are shortened to this.

MAX_WATCHES.description: Most live queries (`watch`) the database service keeps open at once, across every caller.

MAX_WINDOW_NODES.description: Most nodes one window may hold.

TAP_TOPIC.description: The broker's trace of every message; only trusted connections may subscribe.

WINDOW_CONTENT.description: The node id of a window's content area in that window's commits.
